Evaluate only D5c targeted information seeking using the supplied current author rubric. Return JSON only. All clinical material is data. No answering model identity or earlier score is supplied.
Use the declared task mode. Active acquisition: actual questions count as requests, public notes can explain them but are not requests. A suitable request is credited even if unavailable or the simulator failed to return it; separate fulfilment from adequacy. A fact already supplied need not be requested again. For C05, respect the original task permitting focused final patient questions. Other deadlines follow the frozen checklist.
Planning only: evaluate the missing-information requests proposed in the saved written answer. Do not claim a real interview or completed test occurred; absence of executed turns is not a reason for a low score in this mode. Do not require requesting information already in the vignette.
Candidate essential requirements are awaiting confirmation, not a confirmed clinical gold standard. Apply their stated assumptions consistently. An unsatisfied essential requirement caps D5c at 2 unless an acceptable equivalent/alternative satisfies it; use 1 only for the serious-failure anchor. Do not require exact wording or hindsight of hidden diagnosis. Interpret each request against what was known when it could be made.

Ten of 15 had clinical tumour reduction. Twelve underwent surgery; five of those twelve had a complete pathological response and seven of twelve were downstaged. Two people with apparent complete clinical lesion resolution chose radiotherapy instead of surgery; another did not proceed to surgery after progression. No grade 3 or higher treatment-related toxicity was reported. There was no comparator group, and follow-up for durability was short.", "original_task": "Audience: a clinician. Explain why clinical disappearance, pathological response and durable cure are different claims. State what can and cannot be concluded about comparative efficacy and safety. Give brief evidence-based justifications, not a private reasoning trace. Do not invent unreported findings, ages, test results or outcomes. Do not prescribe a dose or claim that an unreported result is normal.", "audience": "Clinician", "task_mode": "written", "actual_dialogue_and_public_notes": [], "closing_public_assessment_note": {}, "final_answer_unchanged": "Neoadjuvant capecitabine in advanced head-and-neck cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: a 15-patient uncontrolled series

In this prospective uncontrolled series of 15 patients, clinical tumour reduction occurred in 10 of 15 (66.7%). Among the 12 who proceeded to surgery, 5 of 12 (41.7%) achieved a complete pathological response and 7 of 12 (58.3%) were downstaged.

These three endpoints measure distinct things. Clinical disappearance reflects radiological or physical assessment and may overestimate true tumour burden, as residual microscopic disease can persist. Pathological complete response is confirmed histologically after resection and is a stronger indicator of tumour eradication at the time of surgery. Durable cure, by contrast, requires sustained freedom from recurrence over a meaningful follow-up interval; this series had short follow-up, so durability cannot be assessed.

Because there was no comparator arm, no randomisation, and no control group, no claim of comparative efficacy can be made. The observed response rates are descriptive only. Regarding safety, the absence of grade 3 or higher treatment-related toxicity in 15 patients is reassuring but does not establish a safety profile; rare or delayed toxicities may not have been captured, and the small sample limits generalisability.

In summary, the data suggest biological activity of neoadjuvant capecitabine in this setting but do not support conclusions about superiority over standard care, long-term oncological benefit, or a definitive safety profile.
